coverage: Pier & Point covers four sites on San Francisco's central waterfront: Mission Rock, Mission Bay, Pier 70 and Potrero Power Station. A parcel that is not in this data is outside coverage, not "no activity".

record.name: Five88 (Mission Bay South Block 7 West)
record.summary: A four-story, ~230,000 sq ft affordable apartment building at 588 Mission Bay Blvd North (Mission Bay South Block 7 West) with 200 affordable apartments (SocketSite, 2015) and over 10,000 sq ft of ground-floor retail, developed by Related California in partnership with Chinatown Community Development Center and designed by David Baker Architects. SocketSite reported in January 2015 that groundbreaking was expected in April 2015, and the architect's own project page lists the building as completed in 2017.

changes.text: The record now says 200 affordable apartments as SocketSite reported them (not '198 plus a manager's unit') and treats SocketSite's January 2015 piece as a forecast of an April 2015 groundbreaking, not a report that it happened; the 'under construction' milestone was removed. Entries that said Blue Bottle Coffee was announced, and that Proper Foods and Bank of America opened, were reworded to say only that a sign permit exists. Entries about the teller-line, address-correction, excavation and sliding-door permits now say what the DBI permit records show (issued or completed, and which permit). The Assessor details now reflect the 2023-2025 rolls (year built 2017, 208 units), the NAIP aerial image credit names the Farm Production and Conservation Business Center, and the Wikimedia photo credit no longer names an author or a flight that the file page does not state.

changes.text: A permit to clarify the support structure of the solar hot water storage tank was recorded complete on 2017-02-13.
An over-the-counter alterations permit was issued on 2021-03-26 documenting the as-built relocation of 3 LED wall horn/strobes.
An over-the-counter alterations permit was recorded complete on January 7, 2022.
Sprinkler work on the ground floor, relocating 36 sprinklers and adding 20, was valued at $28,000 when filed in May 2019.
Work to add an auto sliding door and upgrade floor finishes at the main entry was permitted, with a revised cost of $10,000.
Sprinkler work on the first floor to match a tenant improvement layout was valued at $4,575 when the permit was issued.
Work to relocate pendent fire sprinkler heads to meet new ceiling heights and walls was valued at $15,000.
Work to install one 4-ton heat pump with refrigerant lines and ductwork was valued at $15,000 on the June 2022 permit.
Replacing insulation and fire-rated drywall in units 135, 134 and 136 and a common hallway was valued at $12,000.
Work to modify the building's fire alarm system was valued at $16,140 on the permit issued in January 2021.
A permit issued June 24, 2022 valued at $15,476 covers adding 4 ceiling-mounted fire alarms to the ground-floor space.

A 2025-10-31 permit to excavate and shore tunnels beneath the podium slab had been tagged with a status, reverting the building's status on the timeline years after its real completion. Three tenants sourced only to permit filing dates (Proper Foods, Bank of America, Blue Bottle Coffee) are removed from the confirmed tenant list until a source actually states they are open, announced or closed.

changes.text: A February 2021 sign permit named Blue Bottle Coffee at this building; it does not show the tenant was announced or open.
A medical/dental clinic buildout at 1365 Fourth Street was permitted for $75,000.
A ground-floor retail space was permitted to convert to a food service establishment for $175,000.
DBI permit 202205194650 (completed 2022-09-01): "sign b vinyl window logo proper foods". A $500 sign permit does not state that the business opened, so the tenant is not listed as confirmed.

DBI permit 201909121489 (issued 2019-09-12): "administrative permit only: address correction for pa#201905302080 from 1345 4th street to "1375 4th street."". It corrects the address on one permit (the fitness-studio tenant improvement), not the address of the building, which is 588 Mission Bay Blvd North.
A ground-floor space was permitted for restroom, breakroom and teller-line improvements, for $600,000.
DBI permit 201902284052, issued 2019-04-18 with no completion recorded, is for tenant improvements changing a space at 1335 Fourth Street from retail sales to a lending institution.
The plumbing project's permit lists 200 existing and 200 proposed apartment units, unchanged.
A permit was issued in October 2025 to excavate tunnels under the podium slab and replace plumbing trunk lines, valued at $8,000,000.
The plumbing trunk-line replacement project's excavation and shoring permit was issued.
The building's laundry room was permitted for structural and roofing repairs, plus mechanical work, for $350,000.
The laundry room's structural, roofing and mechanical repair permit was recorded complete.

DBI permit 201911016173 (issued 2019-11-12; never marked complete): "install 1 illuminated single faced wall signs "bank of america"". A sign permit does not state that the branch opened, so the tenant is not listed as confirmed.
A ground-floor fitness studio with retail was permitted for $300,000, including HVAC and two ADA bathrooms.
The ground-floor fitness studio's permit was recorded complete.
A city permit records the building as having 200 apartment units.

DBI permit 201908088230, issued 2019-08-08 with no completion recorded, covers shop drawings to install a teller line and references permit 201902284052, a 2019 change of use to a lending institution. It does not show that a bank branch was completed.
A solar hot water heating system was installed for $310,000.
The solar hot water heating system's permit was recorded complete.
A vacant ground-floor retail space was divided into two retail spaces for $185,000.
A ground-floor space was built out for a new cafe for $400,000.
The new cafe's ground-floor buildout was completed.

Two tenant entries were dropped as duplicates, not errors. Permits 201911016171 (two illuminated wall signs) and 201911016173 (one illuminated wall sign) were the same signage buildout for the same Bank of America branch at 588 Mission Bay Blvd North, filed minutes apart on 2019-11-01 and both issued 2019-11-12; the more specific entry was kept. Likewise permits 202205194649 (sign A) and 202205194650 (sign B) were the same Proper Food(s) signage buildout at the same address, filed 12 minutes apart on 2022-09-01; the 'Proper Foods' entry (open, dated) was kept and the 'Proper Food' entry (announced, undated) dropped, rather than show the same tenant twice under two spellings and two statuses. Permits are read one at a time, with no check for duplicates across permits, so this is a known gap rather than a one-off mistake.

open_questions: Precise completion month not found -- David Baker Architects' own project page gives only 'Completed 2017'.

DataSF's Assessor tax roll records no year_property_built for this parcel (blklot 8711226), consistent with this record's map note; the 2017 completion year rests on the architect's project page rather than a public assessor or permit record.

A November 2016 UCSF news item describes the building as still welcoming applications ahead of opening, consistent with a 2017 (rather than the originally targeted September 2016) completion, but doesn't itself give a specific opening date.
Blue Bottle Coffee's confirmed opening date is not given by any source found (status: announced).

No date found for Blue Bottle Coffee's announced opening (588 Mission Bay Blvd North): the only source is a DBI sign permit, whose own text (a one-line sign description) carries no date; Pier & Point's retail list also has no opening date, as expected for an announced tenant with no confirmed opening yet.

2026-09-29: no source was found reporting that Five88's groundbreaking actually took place in April 2015 (SocketSite's January 2015 piece is a forecast); the unit count is 200 affordable apartments per SocketSite, while the DataSF Assessor roll lists 208 units on the 2023-2025 rolls (year built 2017), which is not reconciled.

record.notes: Five88 (Mission Bay South Block 7 West), 588 Mission Bay Blvd North -- 200 affordable apartments (SocketSite, Jan 2015), a four-story, ~230,000 sq ft mixed-use development with over 10,000 sq ft of ground-floor retail, 52 parking spaces and 306 bike spaces. Developed by Related California in partnership with Chinatown Community Development Center; architect David Baker + Partners. Targets households averaging up to 60% of Area Median Income, with 50 of the 200 units reserved with a preference for university/healthcare employees. SocketSite (Jan 2015) reported groundbreaking as expected in April 2015 with occupancy targeted for September 2016 (no report of the groundbreaking itself found); DataSF's Assessor roll (wv5m-vpq2) lists blklot 8711226 with year_property_built 2017 and 208 units on the 2023-2025 rolls (no year built or units on earlier rolls). Explicitly identified as 'Block 7 West' in SocketSite's own January 2015 coverage, which is how this record was matched to the plan's '7W' label after an error in fitting the plan drawing to the map had placed that label on the wrong side of 4th St (see the changelog). DataSF's Building Footprints layer records no footprint of its own for this parcel (the one fragment intersecting it, mblr SF8711227, actually belongs to the neighboring Family House parcel at their shared boundary) -- confirmed visually against satellite imagery -- so this record uses the real Assessor parcel boundary directly, the same treatment as Mission Bay Block 6 East on this same block face.
